raw_response:
I am 36 years old and I have been working the land since I was a boy. My father taught me everything I know — I never went to school, so I cannot read the words on the fertilizer bags, but I know the colors and the pictures, and I remember what works. I have about 8 mu of flat land, good soil, same as my neighbors in the village.

This year I will grow winter wheat and summer maize on all 8 mu. That is what my family has always done. I thought about cotton, but cotton needs too much picking and the price goes up and down like a crazy person. Wheat and maize are my insurance — even if one is not so good, the other usually saves us. I need the wheat for our own flour, and the maize I can sell to the grain station or feed to the pigs.

For the wheat, I will sow in early October, right after the National Day holiday. I will hire Old Wang to bring his rotary tiller — 50 yuan per mu, same price as last year. I will buy improved wheat seed from the village supply shop. This year they have a kind in a bag with a red stripe; my neighbor across the road used it last year and said it stood up well to the wind. Before sowing I will spread about one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu. I do not know the numbers on the bag, but the shopkeeper said it is the one for wheat, and I have used it before. When the wheat turns green in March, if it looks yellow and weak, I will scatter some ammonium bicarbonate that I have left over from last year — maybe half a bag per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once in March when it wakes up, and once more in April before the ears come out. The electricity for pumping water is expensive now, but three times is what my father did and what everyone in the village does. For spraying, I will do herbicide once in early spring, insecticide twice for aphids, and if I see rust like two years ago, I will spray fungicide once.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I have only a few days before I must plant the maize. There is no time to plow — I will sow directly into the wheat stubble, no-tillage, same as everybody. I will buy hybrid maize seed, Denghai 605, one small package per mu from the shop. The hybrid seed costs more, but if you save your own seed it grows badly, so I buy new every year. I will put compound fertilizer in the furrow with the seed. The maize grows fast in summer. I will irrigate twice if the sky does not give us rain — once when the plants are knee-high, and once when they flower and make pollen. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for the corn borer. That pest ate too much two years ago and I lost money.

I am hoping for about 900 jin per mu of wheat and 1000 jin per mu of maize. Last year was too dry and I got less, but this spring the wells are not as low, so maybe it will be better. I do not have much cash in my pocket, so I cannot buy the most expensive inputs, but I know that if I do what my neighbors do and do not take stupid risks, there will be enough flour for my family and maybe a little money left to fix the roof.
